label: rare original-phase feature, enriched after n/q inputs in sequences starting with 3
explanation: Very sparse (0.03% of steps). 96% of mass is in the original phase at t>=3, never at t=0-1, and almost never in the copy phase. It is strongly enriched when the previous input is n (12.5x) or q (8.4x), when prev2 is n/o/q, and when the sequence starts with 3 (13.7x); it often fires on the token right after an "o n" or "n q" run, e.g. "3 j o n [q k o]". All of these contexts are common, though, and the feature fires on only a tiny fraction of them (precision under 10%). It appears to depend on a specific hidden-state configuration that no simple token predicate captures. Best predicate: dev F1 0.13.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=3 (+4.65), prev_tok=n (+3.57), orig1=3 (+3.55), orig1=i (+3.55), prev2_tok=n (+3.51), prev_tok=q (+3.40). Lower it: phase=2 (-4.94), prev3_tok=r (-2.69), orig0=n (-2.53), orig0=1 (-2.16).
